headline: Football star Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez marry in Portugal
summary: The couple tied the knot in a private civil ceremony in Cascais, attended by their five children.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo and longtime partner Georgina Rodriguez have officially become husband and wife following a private civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal.
The couple announced the news via a joint Instagram post featuring matching gold wedding rings, which quickly garnered over a million likes.
The intimate event was attended by their five children, keeping with Georgina's preference for private celebrations over large parties.
Ronaldo and Georgina first met in 2016 at a Gucci shop in Madrid where Georgina worked, eventually going public with their relationship a year later.
The couple shares a family of five children, including Alana Martina and Bella Esmeralda, as well as Cristiano Jr, Mateo, and Eva.
The 41-year-old Al-Nassr star and five-time Ballon d'Or winner recently confirmed that the 2026 World Cup will be his final tournament.
Ronaldo has already made history as the first player to score in six different World Cup editions.
caption:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have officially tied the knot!

Cristiano Ronaldo and longtime partner Georgina Rodriguez have officially become husband and wife following a private civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal.

The couple announced the news via a joint Instagram post featuring matching gold wedding rings, which quickly garnered over a million likes.

The intimate event was attended by their five children, keeping with Georgina's preference for private celebrations over large parties.

Ronaldo and Georgina first met in 2016 at a Gucci shop in Madrid where Georgina worked, eventually going public with their relationship a year later.

The couple shares a family of five children, including Alana Martina and Bella Esmeralda, as well as Cristiano Jr, Mateo, and Eva.

The 41-year-old Al-Nassr star and five-time Ballon d'Or winner recently confirmed that the 2026 World Cup will be his final tournament.

Ronaldo has already made history as the first player to score in six different World Cup editions.

headline_marked: At least 14 [[injured in Jubo Dal-Chhatra Dal clashes]] in Dhaka’s New Market
headline: At least 14 injured in Jubo Dal-Chhatra Dal clashes in Dhaka’s New Market
summary: The violence erupted Tuesday evening over alleged extortion from footpath vendors and control of the area near Balaka Cinema Hall.
details: At least 14 people were injured in clashes between activists of Jubo Dal’s New Market unit and Chhatra Dal members from Dhaka College in the New Market area on Tuesday evening.
The conflict began around 7:30 pm near Balaka Cinema Hall. Witnesses say the clashes were triggered by alleged extortion from footpath vendors and disputes over control of the area.

According to reports, Jubo Dal activists attempted to collect money from vendors, which was resisted by Dhaka College Chhatra Dal members. This led to an altercation and subsequent attacks using sticks and knives.
The violence spread to Bashundhara Goli near Priyangan Market, where further clashes, vandalism, and counter-attacks occurred, causing widespread panic in the area.
Eight injured from the Chhatra Dal side were identified, including Joint Convener Prince Khandaker and several other members. Six injured from the Jubo Dal side were also identified.
The injured were initially treated at Popular Hospital in Dhanmondi before several were moved to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for further care.
DMCH Police Camp In-charge Inspector Md Faruk confirmed that 14 people had arrived for treatment by 11:00 pm, noting that the number of injured could increase.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Sheikh Zahidul Islam confirmed the clashes and stated that the situation was under police control by 11:30 pm. Police are now investigating the incident to take legal action.
caption:
At least 14 people injured as Jubo Dal and Chhatra Dal clash in Dhaka's New Market over footpath vendor extortion.

At least 14 people were injured in clashes between activists of Jubo Dal’s New Market unit and Chhatra Dal members from Dhaka College in the New Market area on Tuesday evening.

The conflict began around 7:30 pm near Balaka Cinema Hall. Witnesses say the clashes were triggered by alleged extortion from footpath vendors and disputes over control of the area.

According to reports, Jubo Dal activists attempted to collect money from vendors, which was resisted by Dhaka College Chhatra Dal members. This led to an altercation and subsequent attacks using sticks and knives.

The violence spread to Bashundhara Goli near Priyangan Market, where further clashes, vandalism, and counter-attacks occurred, causing widespread panic in the area.

Eight injured from the Chhatra Dal side were identified, including Joint Convener Prince Khandaker and several other members. Six injured from the Jubo Dal side were also identified.

The injured were initially treated at Popular Hospital in Dhanmondi before several were moved to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for further care.

DMCH Police Camp In-charge Inspector Md Faruk confirmed that 14 people had arrived for treatment by 11:00 pm, noting that the number of injured could increase.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Sheikh Zahidul Islam confirmed the clashes and stated that the situation was under police control by 11:30 pm. Police are now investigating the incident to take legal action.
